rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Annual residential rent increases are limited to the lower of 3% or 80% of the CPI change over the most recent 12 months, with no increase allowed if CPI is negative. Owners may petition for relief to obtain a fair and reasonable return, and must give tenants written notice of the Ordinance at lease start or with any rent increase notice.
rules.key_value: Lower of 3% per year or 80% of CPI change; 0% if CPI negative
rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period. If the CPI is negative, no rent increase is permitted.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental property and mobile home spaces; the rent cap does not apply to residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995, or to mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990.
rules.exemptions: Residential buildings constructed after February 1, 1995; mobile home spaces offered for rent after January 1, 1990. Owners may petition the City Manager for a fair-return increase, with a decision due within 60 days of a complete application.
rules.interaction: The document does not discuss the relationship to any state rent cap.
rules.extraction_note: This is a city news release, not the ordinance text. The adoption date is given only as 'Tuesday night' with no calendar date. Annual allowable increases are published by June 30 and take effect September 1. The construction cutoff is based on the construction date, which is mapped to year_built.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may terminate only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in a written notice, and must first give the tenant notice and an opportunity to cure any violation. For no-fault terminations, the owner must either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.key_value: Just cause required after 30 days of tenancy; 3 months relocation assistance or 3 months rent waiver for no-fault terminations
rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Under a no-fault just cause termination, the owner shall either provide 3 months of relocation assistance or waive payment of rent for the final 3 months of the tenancy.
rules.coverage_text: Tenancies of more than 30 days in residential property, excluding housing produced in the last 15 years and other listed exemptions.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable housing; hotel and transient occupancy; hospital and care facilities; dormitories; and other shared living quarters.
rules.interaction: The document does not discuss the relationship to state just cause law.
rules.extraction_note: This is a city news release, not the ordinance text. The adoption date is given only as 'Tuesday night'. The new-construction exemption is a rolling 15-year window, not a fixed date. Owners must notify existing tenants before December 19, 2021, or at lease commencement or renewal.
